## Proof

We have $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ i.i.d. with density $f(x) = e^{-x}$ for $x > 0$, i.e., each $X_i \sim \mathrm{Exp}(1)$ with CDF

$$P(X_i < x) = 1 - e^{-x}, \quad x > 0.$$

Denote $M_n = \max(X_1, \ldots, X_n)$. By independence,

$$P(M_n < a) = P(X_1 < a, \ldots, X_n < a) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} P(X_i < a) = \bigl(1 - e^{-a}\bigr)^n.$$

Setting $a_n = 2 + \log_e n$, we compute

$$e^{-a_n} = e^{-(2 + \log n)} = e^{-2} \cdot e^{-\log n} = \frac{e^{-2}}{n}.$$

Therefore

$$P\bigl(M_n < 2 + \log_e n\bigr) = \left(1 - \frac{e^{-2}}{n}\right)^n.$$

Using the standard limit $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(1 + \tfrac{c}{n}\right)^n = e^{c}$ with $c = -e^{-2}$,

$$\lim_{n \to \infty} P\bigl(M_n < 2 + \log_e n\bigr) = \lim_{n \to \infty}\left(1 - \frac{e^{-2}}{n}\right)^n = e^{-e^{-2}}.$$

This is consistent with the classical extreme-value (Gumbel) result: for i.i.d. exponential(1) variables, $M_n - \log n$ converges in distribution to a Gumbel random variable with CDF $G(y) = \exp(-e^{-y})$, and here $y = 2$, giving $G(2) = e^{-e^{-2}}$.

$$\boxed{\lim_{n \to \infty} P\bigl(X_n < 2 + \log_e n\bigr) = e^{-e^{-2}}}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
